hook: Did the expert say it, deny it or never mention it? Catch the small qualifiers and you will hear the difference.
intro: An interview with the urban climate researcher Dr. Keller about heat protection in cities: what has changed in ten years, why the tropical nights matter, which measures work (trees, green roofs, water features), why old trees cannot simply be replaced, where residents resist, who is most at risk, and what small towns should do. The quiz gives eight statements to mark stimmt (she says it, perhaps in other words), stimmt nicht (she says the opposite or explicitly rejects it) or nicht gesagt (she does not address it). The third answer is where listeners go wrong: a hint is not a statement, and "encouraging first results" is not "proven". Listen for the qualifiers — zumindest auf dem Papier, allerdings weniger, solange, ich will nicht behaupten — each of them is the key to one statement.
tips[0].title: Three answers, three tests
tips[0].text: stimmt: she said it. stimmt nicht: she said the opposite or rejected it. nicht gesagt: she left the point open or never touched it. A question she explicitly leaves open ("ist eine andere Frage") is nicht gesagt — not stimmt nicht, because she denies nothing.
tips[0].trap: Do not mark stimmt nicht because the speaker sounds sceptical. Scepticism without a statement is still nicht gesagt.
tips[0].check.why: She leaves the question open and denies nothing, so the statement is not said.
tips[0].visual.root.q: Did the speaker say it, in other words?
tips[0].visual.root.no.q: Did the speaker say the opposite?
tips[1].title: Qualifiers are the items
tips[1].text: zumindest auf dem Papier (only on paper) · allerdings weniger (less) · solange (only as long as) · ich will nicht behaupten, dass … (I am not claiming). Each qualifier limits or reverses a claim, and the statement is built on exactly that limit.
tips[1].check.why: allerdings nur limits the claim to the city centre, which contradicts ‘everywhere’.
tips[2].title: Plausible is not said
tips[2].text: If you catch yourself thinking "that is probably true", stop: the question is whether SHE said it. Encouraging is not proven; high acceptance under a condition is not general approval.
tips[2].check.why: An indication is not proof, and she does not deny it either; the claim of proof is simply not made.
remember[0]: stimmt = said; stimmt nicht = opposite or rejected; nicht gesagt = left open or never addressed.
remember[1]: Qualifiers (zumindest, allerdings, solange, ich will nicht behaupten) decide the items; plausible ≠ said.
exam: Deciding what an expert said, denied or never mentioned is a core listening skill in the C1 exam — and in every news interview.
